dataset.name: SPRUCE S1 Bog Plant-Available Nutrients Assessed with Ion-Exchange Resins from 2011-2012 in the Southern End of the S1 Bog
description: This data set consists of observations of plant-available nutrients assessed using ion-exchange resin capsules incubated serially in aerobic and anaerobic peat layers beginning in 2011. Data were collected from 2011 to 2012 (prior to the construction of the SPRUCE experimental plots) at the southern end of the S1 Bog at three depths in hollow microtopography only. PVC resin-access tubes (allowing repeated, and undisturbed access to the same soil location over time) were installed across hummock and hollow microtopography in the SPRUCE experimental plots. Resin capsules were placed into contact with the soil at the base of resin-access tubes and incubated in situ for approximately 28 days before collection and replacement with a new resin capsule. The experimental work was conducted in a Picea mariana [black spruce] - Sphagnum spp. bog forest in northern Minnesota, 40 km north of Grand Rapids, in the USDA Forest Service Marcell Experimental Forest (MEF).

measurementTechnique:
Resin-access tube installation
In May, 2011, an array of three resin-access tubes (allowing repeated sampling of the same location over time; WECSA, LLC, Saint Ignatius, MT, USA) were installed at a 30° angle from vertical to reach -10, -30, and -60 cm depths in hollow microtopography in three locations at the south end of the bog near minirhizotrons. In June 2013, arrays of six resin-access tubes were similarly installed across a paired hummock-hollow surface in each of 16 SPRUCE experimental plots (n = 12 tubes per plot, Figs. 2 and 3) to capture microtopographic differences in nutrient availability in two locations in each plot. The resin-access tubes were installed at -10 and -30 cm in the hollows and hummocks, and also at -10 and -30 cm from the hummock surface (~+15 and +5, depending on hummock height, which averaged 25 cm above the hollow surface in sites where resin access tubes were installed).

Resin capsule collection
Plant-available nutrients were assessed biweekly or monthly from May 2011 to July 2012 at the southern end of the S1 bog prior to the construction of the SPRUCE experimental plots.
Please refer to Figure 1. Collection of ion-exchange resin capsules from resin-access tubes and placement into individual plastic bags in cooler. Replacement of new ion-exchange resin capsule at the end of resin-access tube. Note that nitrile gloves are worn to avoid resin contamination.

Resin capsule analysis
Collected resin capsules were rinsed free of peat using distilled water, air-dried, and serially extracted three times with 2 M KCl (for a total of 60 ml) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL; Fig. 3). Extractant was filtered through Whatman #1 filter paper, frozen at -20°C, and thawed before analysis for NH4+, NO3-, and PO4- on a Lachat autoanalyzer (Lachat QuikChem 8500, Hach Company, Loveland, CO).
Resin capsules that were not incubated in situ were kept in a refrigerator until collection of the incubated resins, and then rinsed, air-dried, and serially extracted in a similar manner to incubated resins to serve as blanks.

Nutrient adsorption calculation
Nutrient adsorption was blank-corrected and standardized per unit of resin capsule surface area (11.4 cm2) and per a 30-day interval. The standardized data are reported here.
